subject: Segmentation & Stateful Firewall: IaC module bundling and CI handoff
messages:
From: alex.morales@acmeops.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-infra@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Segmentation plan & handoff: Terraform + Helm + Ansible artifacts

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Per our call, I'm attaching the initial proposal for the VPC segmentation pattern we plan to enforce across AcmeCorp private deployments. High-level asks:

- A minimal, opinionated Terraform module that establishes cross-subnet routing + egress ACLs.
- A corresponding Helm chart overlay for service mesh zone-labeling.
- An Ansible role for stateful firewall rules (jump host + bastion ACLs) that can be run during on-prem site prep.

We're aiming for a sprint handoff to Redwood's PrivDeploy CI on May 20th. Could your team confirm the required artifact conventions and expected CI gate checks so we can align our repo layout?

Attachments: segmentation-module-proposal.md (outline), stateful-fw-ansible-role.tar.gz (role stub), ci-pipeline-template.yml

Appreciate a terse checklist of acceptance criteria so our SREs can lock the templates down.

Best,
Alex Morales
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
AcmeCorp

---

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: alex.morales@acmeops.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Segmentation plan & handoff: Terraform + Helm + Ansible artifacts

Alex — thanks for the materials. Quick response and next steps from Redwood's side:

1) Artifact conventions
   - Terraform: single root module for networking (modules/networking/segmentation) with provider-agnostic variables and a tfstate locking expectation (we expect your team to enable remote state backend; CI will validate backend config).
   - Helm: overlay charts under charts/segmentation-overlay with values.schema.json and explicit hooks disabled by default.
   - Ansible: roles/seg-fw with meta/main.yml declaring dependencies and a Molecule test scenario (we'll gate on a passing molecule converge).

2) CI gate checklist (we'll enforce in PR pipeline)
   - terraform fmt & validate pass; plan output has no changes if run against a dry-run env
   - helm lint && schema validation against our overlay rules
   - ansible-lint + molecule converge in the CI matrix (non-root execution)
   - evidence artifacts: plan.out, helm-values.json, molecule-report.xml attached to the PR build

3) Security expectations
   - No embedded secrets in any templates; use provider-agnostic secret references (KMS/HSM placeholders).
   - Default deny egress for management plane; explicit egress rules only after PR justification.

We'll set up a short onboarding PR template and a CI baseline job in the privdeploy repo. Karthik and Marissa will take the technical review; I'll track stakeholder sign-off.

Can you confirm your repo URL and whether you want Redwood to open a branch with starter scaffolding?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Staff, Platform Security & PrivDeploy
Redwood Inference

---

From: alex.morales@acmeops.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-infra@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 13:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation plan & handoff: Terraform + Helm + Ansible artifacts

Kimberly, Karthik —

Repo is private: git@github.com:acmeops/privdeploy-modules.git. We can either invite a Redwood bot or you can open a branch if that's easier. We prefer Redwood to open a starter branch so the scaffolding matches your CI expectations exactly.

Couple of clarifications:
- For stateful firewall rules, we have mandatory logging and connection-tracking labels. Are there specific molecule scenarios we should include to prove conntrack behavior under load?
- Egress: we'll keep default deny for user-facing subnets, but need a documented egress carveout for updates (package repos). Is a documented exception with expire-on-date enough for the CI gate?

I attached an updated segmentation proposal (small edits) and a tiny Ansible role tarball with a basic molecule.yml.

Thanks — will stand by for the branch scaffolding.

Alex

---

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, alex.morales@acmeops.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Segmentation plan & handoff: Terraform + Helm + Ansible artifacts

Alex / team —

Thanks for the repo pointer and the clarifications. Action items from our side (I'll own the branch + initial CI jobs):

- I'll create the scaffold branch: redwood/scaffold/seg-fw-2025-05-12 on your repo and push a starter pipeline that runs: terraform fmt/validate/plan (with plan output capture), helm lint & values schema check, ansible-lint, and a constrained molecule converge using a lightweight container scenario.
- Molecule scenario: include a connection-tracking smoke test (we'll run conntrack -L inside a containerized netns) and assert that logging hooks are present. That should be sufficient for the CI gate; full load testing will be a separate manual job we can run outside PRs.
- Egress carveouts: yes — documented exception with expire-on-date and a corresponding Jira ticket ID will satisfy the gate. We'll add a linter that fails the PR if expire-on-date is missing.
- Secrets: we'll add a CI check that rejects commits with common secret fingerprints and fail fast.

Kimberly / Marissa: I'll send a PR with the starter branch + pipeline later today and tag you for the technical review. Alex: please add a small README at repo root with quick setup steps and a point of contact for on-site engineers.

If there are any policy exceptions (for example, on metal where remote state is not possible), flag them early and we'll route through our private deployment exceptions process (requires security sign-off).

I'll follow up with the PR link once created.

— Karthik
Senior SRE, PrivDeploy Runtime
Redwood Inference
